title: Why 2100 skips leap day
idea: Why the year 2100 will not have a February 29

lines.text: Earth needs about *365 and a quarter.*

scenes.kicker: But that is slightly too much.

lines.text: About *11 minutes* too much, every year.

scenes.kicker: By 1582 it had grown to ten days.

lines.text: century years *skip* it, unless they divide by 400.

p.items: EVERY 4TH YEAR = LEAP, CENTURY YEARS = SKIP, DIVIDES BY 400 = LEAP

hooks: Leap years are *not* every four years.
A Pope once *deleted* ten days from the calendar.
caption: 2100 divides by 4 and it still is not a leap year. This is the 400-year-old rule behind it.

sources.claim: Leap year rule: divisible by 4, except century years not divisible by 400. 1900 and 2100 are not leap years, 2000 was
A year (tropical year) is about 365.2422 days. The old 365.25-day average ran about 0.0078 days long, which is about 11 minutes a year
Ten days were dropped in October 1582: 15 October followed 4 October

notes: "365 and a quarter" is the rounded figure the old calendar assumed. The 11 minutes is my conversion of 0.0078 days. The reform was ordered by Pope Gregory XIII.
